clue.text: A miserable pretence that queue moves at a great pace

parts.note: a crocodile is a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs, i.e. a queue on the move
to tear is to rush along at speed

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that a queue is racing ahead, which is plainly a sad sham.
explanation.walkthrough: A crocodile is the British word for a file of schoolchildren walking two by two.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincere weeping is a show of grief put on for effect, a sorrowful sham.

clue.text: Need to change lire but it's been put up again

indicators.note: letters that need to change must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A currency conversion is needed for old Italian money, though the building has been reconstructed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something constructed a second time has been erected once more.

clue.text: Bird with egg — cackle it's making!

indicators.note: making signals the letters are put together into something new

parts.note: an egg is O-shaped
the words cackle and it, with the 's read as is, a link

explanation.surface: A hen lays an egg and cackles over what it has produced.
explanation.definitionFit: A small crested Australian parrot, a type of bird.

clue.text: Garden product — it can be a hazard

indicators.note: a product is something made from raw material, here the letters reworked

explanation.surface: A garden chemical that might be hazardous.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazard is a risk or peril.

clue.text: Cut ornamental tree with bark that's dead

indicators.note: bark wraps round a tree, so the word for dead encloses the tree

parts.note: the late person is one who has died
the acer, or maple, is planted for its decorative leaves

explanation.surface: Someone cuts down a decorative tree whose bark has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bark' is a container indicator here: the covering of a tree, so the word for dead wraps the tree's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear or gash the flesh is to wound it.

clue.text: Both out to secure right to beat

indicators.note: securing something means holding it inside
out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Both are out to fix the right to beat someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges BOTH into THOB; 'to secure' holds R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To pulsate strongly, as a heart does, is to pound.

clue.text: Girl lied about getting worms

definitions.note: plural in the clue; the answer names one such creature, used here as the class

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around

explanation.surface: A girl lied about having worms.
explanation.definitionFit: The phylum of segmented creatures such as earthworms and leeches.

clue.text: Horse raced around the ring, after fruit

indicators.note: the horse colour comes after the fruit

parts.note: the strawberry is a soft red fruit

indicators.note: the word for raced goes around the ring letter

parts.note: raced means ran
a ring is O-shaped

explanation.surface: A horse raced around the ring after some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse with a chestnut coat flecked with white hairs.

clue.text: As dinner option?

parts.note: a traditional northern English dish of offal stewed with onions offered as a dinner choice; the clue words also rearrange to give the dish's letters

explanation.surface: Something suggested for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The three words of the clue are an exact anagram of the dish, a hidden bonus with no indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Cow's stomach lining cooked with onions in milk is a classic British supper.

clue.text: Has a one-way crossing

parts.note: a river that Caesar crossed in 49 BC, committing himself to civil war; crossing it now means passing a point of no return

explanation.surface: A road or bridge that only lets traffic go one way.
explanation.definitionFit: The river's name stands for a decisive step that cannot be undone, a crossing with no way back.

clue.text: Public officer finding love in a secret place

indicators.note: the letter for love goes inside the word for the out-of-the-way spot

parts.note: a corner is a hidden, out-of-the-way spot
love is nil in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: An official discovers romance tucked away somewhere private.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who holds inquests into sudden deaths is a public office holder.

clue.text: Soldier with monarch on the vessel

parts.note: a private is a soldier of the lowest rank
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: A soldier and the queen are aboard the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An armed ship privately owned but licensed by government to attack enemy shipping.

clue.text: Wobble perilously, losing front brake going downhill

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped from the jumble
something moving perilously is all over the place, so the letters are jumbled
front of the word brake means its first letter only

explanation.surface: A cyclist wobbles dangerously when the front brake fails on a descent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perilously' jumbles WOBBLE; 'losing' drops B, the letter picked by 'front' from 'brake'.
explanation.definitionFit: Going downhill takes you to a lower place, further down.

clue.text: Win a race in a scramble

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the famous Isle of Man motorbike race

indicators.note: a scramble mixes things up, so the two little words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone wins a race that was a mad scramble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scramble' jumbles IN A into AIN. The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: To win something is to achieve or reach it.

clue.text: Street with right turn bad to get across

parts.note: eggs addle when they go rotten

explanation.surface: Someone finds a turning off the high street a poor route over to the other side.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit or stand with a leg on each side of something is to span it.

clue.text: Former queen making use of a system of laws plus military force

parts.note: lex is Latin for law
plus means and
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: A past queen relied on the legal system and the army.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward VII's consort, Queen of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: To receive decoration, change trains and return first class

indicators.note: change signals rearranging the letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: return signals the letters are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first class, with 1 as I

explanation.surface: To get an award, change trains and travel back first class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges TRAINS into INTARS; 'return' turns AI into IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood inlay, or a knitting technique with patterns of coloured yarn, is ornamentation.

clue.text: It's a waste of time by the way

definitions.text: It's a waste of time by the way

parts.words: It's a waste of time by the way
parts.note: a passing remark reads as idling along the road, wasting time on the way

explanation.surface: An aside mentioning that something is pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Loitering is lingering slowly on one's route, frittering time away.

clue.text: Line up on liner for prayers

definitions.note: plural, while the answer is a mass noun for devotional services

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a row is a line
a liner is a ship

explanation.surface: Passengers queue up on a cruise ship for a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious devotion, acts of adoration and prayer offered to God.

clue.text: Bugbear to slip a shirt on ?

indicators.note: the shirt letter is placed onto the front of the word for the slip

parts.note: a T is a T-shirt
a slip is a mistake

explanation.surface: Something irritating about having to slip on a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear is a source of dread or fear, an object of fright.

clue.text: Concerned with how you look? Get up later — around half nine

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means reading upwards, backwards
the word later goes around the selected letters
half of the word nine means its first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone told to get up later around half past nine is worried about appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get up' reverses the whole assembly, not just 'later'; the result means relating to the eye, hence the question about how you look.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye, the organ of sight.

clue.text: Foreign dynasty recorded in a Norman church

indicators.note: recorded in says the letters are written within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A foreign ruling family is listed in a Norman church's records.
explanation.definitionFit: The Qing dynasty that ruled China from 1644 to 1912 came from Manchuria.

clue.text: Breathing spaces

parts.note: read literally, the spaces through which we breathe: the nostrils

explanation.surface: Short rests or pauses.
explanation.definitionFit: The anatomical term for the nostrils, openings through which air is drawn.

clue.text: River trip on Sunday

indicators.note: the word for trip is set on after the Sunday letter, so it comes second

parts.note: a tour is a trip

explanation.surface: Taking a day out by the river on Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of several English waterways, including one in Kent and one in Dorset.

clue.text: Mineral free at bar, with ales

indicators.note: free signals the letters are loosened and rearranged

explanation.surface: Drinks are free at the bar, along with some beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine-grained white form of gypsum or calcite, a stone used for carving.

clue.text: Love to have chorus dancing in shade of yellow

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, written O

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and change places

explanation.surface: A loved one gets a chorus line to dance in yellow costumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a yellowish-brown earth pigment, and the adjective describes that tint.

clue.text: Adze can turn out spectacular finish

indicators.note: to turn out is to emerge in a new form, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: A woodworker's adze can produce a striking finish on timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso solo passage near the end of a concerto movement, a showy flourish.

clue.text: By inexplicable means turns up with a really different appearance

indicators.note: giving letters a different appearance means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone shows up looking completely changed by magic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different appearance' rearranges TURNSUP and AREALLY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Done beyond natural laws, by mysterious powers that cannot be explained.
